name: Custom
summary: Keep your own in-game aim settings (like sensitivity and FOV) and copy them into the Config. Only for games that support it.

where.text: Edit your Config (pencil icon), go to its Game Settings section and choose Custom, if the game has it. Then copy your game's aim settings, and its scope settings, into the Config.

citations.quote: To edit the current Config, press the pencil icon.
When a weapon group is enabled, the user will be able to change the current sight to match theirs from the game settings section:
citations.note: Where the guide calls Game Settings a section of the Config.

citations.quote: Game Settings support includes three different synchronization methods: Standard, Custom, and Manual.
This is the default option for controller Configs when custom is available for the game.
To use, copy your game's aim settings into your Config:
Scope settings as well:

definition.text: Custom lets you choose your game's aim settings, including Hip and ADS sensitivity, per-scope sensitivity and field of view (FOV). You then copy them into your Config.

citations.quote: Custom is a powerful synchronization option that let's you choose your game's aim settings including:
Hip and ADS sensitivity
Per-scope sensitivity
Field-of-view (FOV)
To use, copy your game's aim settings into your Config:

plainWords.text: A Config then works with different in-game aim settings without changes. XIM calls this highly beneficial for Configs where you aim with a gamepad, and also valuable for mouse Configs that use Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB).

citations.quote: This means a Config can work with different in-game aim settings without modification. This is highly beneficial for controller Configs, but, also valuable for mouse Configs that are using Simulate Analog Behavior.
Or, if you are a controller gamer (and the game has support for it), aim is customized in your game and settings are copied to your Config.

plainWords.text: Your custom in-game settings change the game's maximum turn speed.

citations.quote: Custom in-game settings affects the maximum turn speed of the game.

plainWords.text: The aiming stick deadzone is still set only in the Config, not in game. The other required settings, including the in-game deadzone, still apply. Everything else stays default.

citations.quote: Your aiming stick deadzone is customized only though your Config (not via in-game settings):
Follow all additional required aim settings including in-game deadzone. All other aim settings should be default.

plainWords.text: Depending on the game and your aiming sources, it can also bring scope features: a Sight Modifier setting, and scope levels on weapon groups.

citations.quote: If you are using Custom Game Settings, you may have a Sight Modifier setting depending on your current aiming sources.
A scope level can also be assigned (available when using Custom Game Settings) when the group is weapon tracking.
If your Config supports Custom Game Settings and the game has configurable weapon scope levels, you will be able to assign scopes.

guidance.text: It is the default when the game supports Custom and you aim with a gamepad. For Configs that aim with a mouse or gyro, Standard is the default.

citations.quote: This is the default option for controller Configs when custom is available for the game.
This is the default option for all new mouse and gyro Configs.

guidance.text: Switching an existing Config to Custom only works if that Config was made with the required in-game settings.

citations.quote: Enabling custom in-game settings on existing Configs will only work if the Config was created using required in-game settings.

guidance.text: Custom is only there for games that support it. To find out whether a game does, look at the Game Settings of a Config for that game in Manager. On the public copy of XIM's list of game settings, 15 entries say "This game supports Custom In-Game Settings", and each of them also requires Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB). The Destiny 2 entry has no such line. That copy has entries for only about a third of the games in its index, and the list does not say whether a game without that line has Custom.

citations.quote: Game Settings support includes three different synchronization methods: Standard, Custom, and Manual.
This is the default option for controller Configs when custom is available for the game.
This game supports Custom In-Game Settings. Setting values in green can be customized when using this feature.
citations.note: From the Apex Legends (ALC) entry, one of 15 entries with this line in the public copy, whose entries stop at FragPunk. The Destiny 2 entry has no such line.

citations.quote: Input Requirements: This game has additional input requirements that must be observed in order to play. With a XIM MATRIX, it is required that Simulate Analog Behavior (SAB) be enabled.
citations.note: From the Apex Legends (ALC) entry, one of 15 entries with this line in the public copy, whose entries stop at FragPunk. The Destiny 2 entry has no such line.

guidance.reasoning: The guide describes Custom as one of a Config's Game Settings methods, available 'when custom is available for the game'. So a Config's own Game Settings is where to see whether its game has it. On the public list, the line that marks Custom support appears in 15 entries, all of which also require SAB, among the entries the public copy has (about a third of the games in its index). No source says whether a game without the line has Custom.
guidance.caveat: This comes from a public copy of XIM's forum list of game settings. It may differ from the current login-walled list, so confirm in Manager (gear icon on the main screen).

confusions.name: Custom smoothing
confusions.note: Your own smoothing values instead of a preset. Unrelated to Custom sync.

confusions.name: Custom Stick Behavior
confusions.note: Replaces the game's built-in thumbstick aim mechanics with your own curve. Unrelated to Custom sync.

confusions.name: Custom (new Config)
confusions.note: The Custom button for building your own Config instead of adding a shared one. Unrelated to Custom sync.
